passage:
A health teacher created a one-week sleep challenge. Students had to put phones away thirty minutes before bed and record how they felt in the morning.
Some students failed after one night. Others found it difficult at first but slept better by the end.
The class discussed why phones were hard to put down. Games, messages, videos, and fear of missing out all played a part.
The challenge did not turn everyone into perfect sleepers, but it made the problem visible.
Sleep is not only a personal weakness. It is affected by design, habits, stress, and social pressure. Rest requires protection.
